subject: general
question: For how many days is the Chhat Puja celebrated?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Four**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chhat Puja is a significant Hindu festival dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and his consort Usha (Chhathi Maiya).
 
• It is celebrated over a period of four days, with each day having its own unique rituals and significance.
 
• The festival is most prominently observed in the Indian states of Bihar, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh, and the country of Nepal.
 
• The four days of Chhat Puja include Nahay Khay, Kharna, Sandhya Arghya, and Usha Arghya.
 
• Devotees observe rigorous fasting, holy bathing, and offer prayers to the setting and rising sun during the festival.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nahay Khay:**

 
 
• The first day of Chhat Puja, where devotees take a holy dip in a river or water body and prepare the traditional meal.
 
• It signifies the beginning of the purification process both physically and spiritually.
 
 
 
• **Kharna:**
 
 
• The second day involves a day-long fast that ends in the evening after performing rituals and offering kheer (a rice pudding) to the deity.
 
• Devotees abstain from drinking water during this fast until the evening rituals are completed.
 
 
 
• **Sandhya Arghya:**
 
 
• The third day, devotees offer arghya (offerings) to the setting sun, followed by a night-long vigil.
 
• This day is marked by the preparation of various traditional delicacies and the gathering of the community for the evening rituals.
 
 
 
• **Usha Arghya:**
 
 
• The fourth and final day involves offering arghya to the rising sun, marking the end of the fasting period.
 
• Devotees break their fast after the morning rituals and share prasad (sacred food) with the community.
